provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Flatwork buyers decide on cracks, tear-out and pour-day worries, so the kit leans on process and repair-versus-replace. No admixture, sealer or stamp-mat brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Tear-out to pour: how a driveway gets replaced
pageStructurePlus.contains: Breaking out the old slab, haul-off, base gravel and compaction, rebar or wire mesh, slab thickness, control joints, and the day the forms come off
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers compare quotes without knowing what's under the slab. Showing the base and reinforcement explains why the cheap bid cracks.

pageStructurePlus.section: Cracked, sunken or spalled: repair or replace
pageStructurePlus.contains: Hairline shrinkage cracks, heaving from tree roots, sunken panels by the garage, salt spalling, resurfacing overlays, and when the slab has to go
pageStructurePlus.why: Most concrete calls start with a crack the owner is worried about. Sorting the cases up front sends the right jobs to the right visit.

pageStructurePlus.section: Apron, curb cut and sidewalk permit
pageStructurePlus.contains: Where the driveway meets the street, who owns the sidewalk panels, the city right-of-way permit, apron thickness and inspection
pageStructurePlus.why: The street end is where permits and inspections bite. Owners trust the contractor who explains it before they ask.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pour day and concrete curing: what to expect
pageStructurePlus.contains: Weather holds, moving cars out, keeping kids and dogs off fresh concrete, when you can walk on it, when you can drive on it, and the first rain
pageStructurePlus.why: Fear of a ruined pour stalls the booking. Plain timing answers make the date easy to commit to.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Resealing intervals, de-icing salt cautions, colour fade in full sun, slip resistance on pool decks, and booking a reseal visit
pageStructurePlus.why: Stamped buyers worry it will look tired in a few years. A care plan page turns that worry into recurring reseal work.

designDirections.name: Pour Schedule
designDirections.bestFor: Flatwork crews doing driveway tear-outs, garage slabs and sidewalks who win on a quick estimate
designDirections.headlineSample: Driveway replacement and concrete flatwork in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Gunmetal and safety orange read like a ready-mix truck, and the mono type gives slab thickness and cure times a spec-sheet feel.

designDirections.name: Fresh Pour
designDirections.bestFor: Contractors whose cracked-to-new driveway pairs and stamped patios are the whole sales pitch
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Brick red and linen sit naturally beside grey, tan and coloured concrete, and slab headings feel poured in place.

designDirections.name: Decorative Slab
designDirections.bestFor: Decorative specialists doing stamped, stained and exposed aggregate driveways and pool decks
designDirections.whyItFits: A white gallery ground and Didone headings let texture and colour in the concrete be the only ornament on the page.

openers.line: Searching concrete contractors in {City}, your listing comes up with a phone number and no site. Someone staring at a cracked driveway wants to see a slab you've poured before they dial.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a driveway buyer would find behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing's link goes to Facebook, where the stamped patio from last month sits under a post about a pump truck. Someone pricing a new driveway needs finishes and a quote form, not a timeline.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest pour they shared.
openers.linkLine: Your concrete work on a page built for the driveway buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing runs on a free builder and the newest driveway on it looks a few seasons old. Concrete is a once-in-twenty-years buy, so people check the contractor is current.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a broken form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same concrete outfit, current and quick to load: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone, your concrete site's call button sits under a banner that won't close. People price driveways standing on the cracked one, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your concrete site, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Right now the only way to get a driveway number from you is a phone call. Plenty of homeowners would rather send the length, the width and a picture of the cracks after dinner.
openers.hook: Check the listing, bios and any site for a quote form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A concrete quote form that asks size, finish and tear-out: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your ashlar-slate stamped patio and the exposed aggregate driveway on Instagram are the posts people save and show their spouse. There's no page that collects them by finish.
openers.hook: Find two finished pours on their grid you could name by pattern or finish. Use one by name if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your concrete jobs sorted by finish: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about a driveway poured the day you promised and a crew that saved the lawn from the truck tracks. That reassurance never reaches anyone off your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about a pour day, cleanup or a crack-free slab. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews beside the driveways they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Once the ground thaws, every concrete contractor in {City} is booked weeks out. The homeowners who find you in late winter are the ones on your first pours.
openers.hook: Use from January through early March in cold climates, or before the summer rains in hot ones. Name the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the first pours of the year: {demo-link}

openers.line: People notice the cracked driveway on Saturday when they're washing the car, which is when you're not answering. A quote request form catches them while they're looking at it.
openers.hook: Call their listed number on a weekend or after six. A generic or full voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A driveway quote request that works on a Saturday: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a concrete finisher. Good finishers check whether an outfit looks steady before they leave their current crew.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story, a help-wanted note or a truck sign. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A concrete company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You pour driveways across the county, but nothing tells a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you'll bring a truck out there. 'Concrete driveway' plus their town is what they type.
openers.hook: Pull the towns from their captions or reviews and use the one furthest from their yard.
openers.linkLine: A concrete page for each town you pour in: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment options on driveways, put it next to the quote form. A full tear-out and stamped replacement is the kind of bill people want spread out before they ask.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing somewhere public. If not, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Driveway financing explained before the quote: {demo-link}

openers.line: The apron and sidewalk at the street usually need a permit and an inspection. Showing your licence and insurance, and that you handle that permit, answers a careful buyer's first question.
openers.hook: Check the state or city contractor registry for a record. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and the apron permit on one concrete page: {demo-link}

openers.line: A new driveway is the most visible job on a street, so I'd guess the house next door calls you a lot. Even they look up the concrete company before calling.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'saw the driveway down the road'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next driveway referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows clean joints and an even finish. A slab like that should be the first thing a stranger sees about you.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished pour and name it exactly: driveway, patio or walk, finish, pattern and town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted has a really even finish.

I looked up concrete contractors in {City} and found {Business Name} on Maps and Instagram, but no site where a homeowner can see driveways by finish and ask for a quote. I built a sample concrete site to show what that could look like, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Should I send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, bumping this in case it got buried. Here's the sample concrete site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It sorts your work by finish, has a quote form that asks driveway size and whether the old slab comes out, and a page on pour day and curing. Not interested? Say so and I'll leave it there.
sequence.call:
"Hi, {Owner}? This is {Your Name}. I build websites for concrete contractors around {City}. I messaged you about a sample driveway site. Did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. I put together a sample concrete site for {Business Name}: stamped, broom and exposed aggregate work sorted by finish, a quote form that asks size and tear-out, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think of it?"
 → let them answer, don't fill the gap
"It runs {Build Range} depending on how many finish and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and edits. For an outfit your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is a fraction of one driveway."
"Want to go through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday after you've cleaned up?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start when it clears and it's live before your first pours."

objections.objection: I'm too busy pouring to deal with a website.
objections.handler: "That's why I built the sample first. You send me pictures of finished slabs from your phone when it suits you; everything else is on me."

objections.objection: My work comes from builders and word of mouth.
objections.handler: "Builder work keeps the trucks rolling. Homeowner driveways pay better per yard, and those people search before they call. The site is how they find you instead of the outfit with the yard sign."
"Great, that's cheaper than me. Happy to hand over the finish gallery and the quote form layout. If it hasn't happened by spring, call me."

objections.objection: It's winter, we can't pour anyway.
objections.handler: "That's the point. The site gets built and found while you can't pour, so the quote requests are waiting when the ground thaws."

objections.objection: People only care about price per square foot.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the buyer who asks what's under the slab. Show them the base, rebar and joints, and your number stops looking high."

objections.objection: I already get leads from a lead site.
objections.handler: "Those driveway leads go to several contractors at once and you pay for every one. Your own site sends that homeowner to one concrete company."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}: a finish gallery, a quote form, a pour-day page and a few town pages. Less than the tear-out on one driveway."

email.subject: Concrete site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, {Your Name} here. I build websites for concrete contractors in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text the link so you can look after the pour. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm clearing out demos this week and the {Business Name} concrete one comes down Friday.

Want me to keep it up? A yes or no is plenty.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, the ground's about to thaw and driveway quote season starts with it. You came to mind.

The sample concrete site is still up and the price hasn't moved: {demo-link}

bullets: Price the gallery by finish: broom, stamped, coloured and exposed aggregate each answer a different buyer and get their own section.
A quote form that asks length, width, tear-out and finish is the most valuable part of the build. Price it on its own line.
Peg the build against the tear-out cost on a single driveway, not against hours.
Add the apron and permit page only for contractors who work at the street; skip it for patio-only crews.
Before-and-after pairs of cracked to new slabs sell harder than any copy; budget the time to pair and caption them.
Charge a little more in freeze-thaw markets, where the repair-versus-replace page carries more of the selling.

lineItems.description: Max with cracked-to-new pairs, pattern names, colour notes and a care line per finish.

lineItems.item: Driveway quote form with size and tear-out
lineItems.description: Max with picture upload, a measuring guide, finish choice and routing to the estimator by town.
Max when it covers each crack type with examples and links to a resurfacing service.
Max when it lists permit steps for several towns and a printable homeowner checklist.
Max when each town page carries its own finished pours and local permit notes.

lineItems.item: Reseal booking page for stamped work
lineItems.description: Max with a past-customer lookup by address and a seasonal booking window.
Max with sidewalk, curb and parking pad references, insurance limits and a bid request form.

whatElseYouSell.name: Pour-day and finished-slab video shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Film one stamped pour from truck to final pattern, then the finished driveway from the drone. Short clips of a pour get watched far longer than a still slab."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the next stamped or coloured pour.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of new driveways
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each finished driveway goes onto your Maps profile with the finish and the town in the caption, so the listing shows fresh concrete every week."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once a new pour is finished and cured enough to shoot.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review texts sent after the slab cures
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A week after the pour, when they've parked on the new driveway for the first time, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Curing-sign stakes and truck door artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Fresh concrete needs a keep-off sign anyway. Put your name and site on it and the whole street reads it for a week."

whatElseYouSell.name: Late-winter driveway replacement push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A February campaign to homeowners whose driveways cracked over the winter books your first pours before anyone else answers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in December, run from February to the first thaw.

whatElseYouSell.name: Mailers to the block after each driveway pour
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every house on the block saw the mixer. A card with the finished driveway and your number lands while they still remember it."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are finished driveways on the site to show.

whatElseYouSell.name: Stamp pattern and colour sample sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and online sheet of your stamp patterns and colours lets homeowners choose before the estimate, and it's what designers and realtors pass around."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, after the finish gallery is live.

withoutAI.route: Ready-mix plant dispatch and contractor pages
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your ready-mix plant takes every order by phone and its site is a map pin. Introduce me and I'll build a concrete order request page for its contractors."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Plants have budgets and every contractor in the region on their books. Your concrete client knows the dispatcher by name.

withoutAI.whoPays: The leveling contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a sunken slab can be lifted instead of replaced, who do you send them to? I'll build their site, and they'll send you the slabs that can't be saved."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Leveling and replacement sit either side of the same decision. Each side refers the other the job it can't do.

withoutAI.whoPays: The pump operator, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pump truck you call for backyard pours works for every contractor in town. They need a booking page more than anyone."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pump operators live on contractor relationships and rarely have a real site. The intro comes from a regular customer.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shop where you buy release powder and colour hardener runs stamping classes and has no class sign-up page. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply stores sell to every decorative contractor around. Their customer list is your prospect list.

withoutAI.route: Asphalt sealcoating outfits that turn away concrete jobs
withoutAI.whoPays: The sealcoater, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Sealcoaters get asked about concrete driveways every week and send them somewhere. Build their site and that somewhere is you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Different surface, same customer and same season. The referral flows both directions.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Managers get tenant complaints about lifted sidewalk panels and cracked parking pads. A repair request page with pictures and priority speeds up every fix."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trip hazards are a liability line for managers, and your concrete client already patches their properties.

withAI.route: Yardage and order assistant for the ready-mix plant
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors type the slab size and thickness and the assistant works out the yards, suggests the mix and books the truck window."
withAI.whyItWorks: Short loads and wrong mixes cost the plant money. A tool that gets orders right keeps contractors calling one plant.

withAI.route: Sunken-slab triage for the leveling crew
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload a picture of the sunken slab and the assistant sorts it: liftable, needs a look, or needs replacing."
withAI.whyItWorks: It saves wasted visits, and the replace pile goes straight to your concrete client.

withAI.route: Class and product helper for the decorative supply store
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors ask the counter which release colour goes with which base colour. An assistant trained on the store's sheets answers at night."
withAI.whyItWorks: Counter staff repeat the same answers all day. The store pays to free them up.

withAI.route: Sidewalk hazard log for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Maintenance techs snap lifted panels on a walk-through and the assistant logs location, severity and a repair estimate request to one concrete contractor."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers need a paper trail on trip hazards. The concrete client gets a steady repair queue.

withAI.route: Bid follow-up for the pump operator
withAI.pitchLine: "Pump requests come in by text at all hours. An assistant confirms the pour address, boom reach and time, and holds the slot."
withAI.whyItWorks: Double-booked pumps cost everyone a pour. A contractor they already serve made the introduction.

withAI.route: HOA driveway and apron rule checker
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents submit driveway widening or colour changes and the assistant checks them against the HOA's surface and width rules first."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards hate resubmissions. A clean first submission saves them a meeting.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for driveway calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Your hands are in wet concrete when the phone rings. The caller gets a text asking for the address, the slab size and whether the old one comes out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business line forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for concrete jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New reviews get a reply drafted that mentions the driveway, the finish and the town, and you approve it from the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten of their past replies for tone. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Driveway price estimator by size and finish
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner enters length, width, broom or stamped, and tear-out yes or no, and sees a range before you drive over. The sticker-shock visits stop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real square-foot prices by finish, tear-out and haul-off rates and the smallest pour they take.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and pour-day balance billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit when the date is booked, balance the evening of the pour, each sent automatically with a card link. No chasing cheques off the dashboard."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Crack picture triage on the quote form
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload pictures of the cracks and the tool sorts them into seal it, resurface it or replace it, so you know which visit to make."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a set of past crack pictures labelled by what was actually done. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rain-delay notice texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When rain or a freeze pushes a pour, every customer on that day gets a text with the new date before they call you to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their schedule in one place and their usual rain-delay wording.

softwareAI.name: Pour calendar with weather holds and truck windows
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Forms, inspection, ready-mix window and pump on one calendar per pour, with a weather hold you can slide in one tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once quote requests are steady. Needs their job stages and how they book trucks today.

softwareAI.name: After-hours driveway call answerer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It picks up at night, asks driveway, patio or sidewalk, rough size and finish, and books the estimate visit. You get a summary at six in the morning."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they trust you. Needs their calendar, service list and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Yardage and truck-order calculator for the crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter slab dimensions and thickness, and the foreman gets yards with waste, rebar count and the order text for the plant. No more short loads."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their waste factor, standard thicknesses and how they order from the plant.

softwareAI.name: Concrete chatbot on finishes, curing and lead times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'when can I park on it' and 'does stamped get slippery' at midnight, from your own care sheet and current schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their care sheet, finish list and lead time, refreshed monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Stamped reseal reminder sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Stamped customers get a reseal reminder when the sealer is due, with a booking link. That's repeat concrete work from driveways you already poured."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a list of past stamped jobs with pour dates and their reseal price.

softwareAI.name: Homeowner pour-day portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The customer approves the pattern and colour, sees the pour date, and gets the keep-off and cure instructions in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the pour calendar in place first.

softwareAI.name: Stamp pattern and colour visualiser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a picture of their driveway and sees it in ashlar slate, cobblestone or plain broom before the estimate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their pattern and colour list and a set of finished jobs to tune against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Commercial flatwork bid packet builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick the sidewalk, curb or pad scope and it assembles the bid: quantities, insurance certificate, references and schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for contractors chasing commercial work. Needs two past bids and their insurance certificate.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote for the driveway walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pace the driveway, say the dimensions, finish and tear-out into the phone, and it drafts the quote with haul-off and apron included."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Aerial-view driveway area drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the address alone it drafts the driveway outline and square footage off aerial imagery, for you to confirm before quoting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a set of past measured driveways to check accuracy. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Reseal route planner for stamped customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Groups booked reseals by neighbourhood so one crew does five stamped driveways in a day instead of crossing town twice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, once reseal bookings come in. Needs their reseal list and crew days.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per yard poured
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each driveway really made per yard once concrete, pump, rebar, dump fees and crew hours are in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of plant tickets, dump receipts and crew hours.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with base, rebar and joint checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before the truck arrives, the foreman logs base depth, compaction, rebar and form height with a picture each, so a crack claim later has a record."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, when they run two crews. Needs their pre-pour checklist and a foreman to test it.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for finishers and laborers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Concrete applicants answer whether they can float and edge, have a licence and can start at six, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they post for finishers. Needs their must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the driveway estimator for flatwork contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One concrete contractor stopped driving to sticker-shock quotes with this driveway estimator. Every flatwork crew in the region has that same wasted evening."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client taught you the square-foot logic and paid for it. The next hundred only need their own prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Applicator locator for a decorative coatings maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners see your stamped colours and ask who installs them. A locator of trained applicators turns that question into jobs for your customers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund channel tools. The concrete client proves you understand the contractor side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A finish gallery, quote form and pour-day page every member concrete company can switch on. It gives members a reason to renew."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One agreement reaches dozens of contractors who already trust the association.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label concrete template for marketing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with a concrete client rebuild the same quote form every time. License a flatwork template with finishes and pour-day pages done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship and want speed. You sell them the finished part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents apply for the sidewalk replacement cost-share, upload the cracked panel and get matched to approved concrete contractors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Cities run these programs on paper. Your concrete client already knows the inspectors and the program rules.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Subdivision flatwork scheduling for production builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Driveways and walks on fifty lots, each waiting on grade and inspection. A scheduling board shared with the flatwork sub keeps closings on time."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Late driveways delay closings, which builders feel in cash. The concrete client is the sub who would use it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every concrete resurfacing territory needs a crack guide, a quote form and town pages routed to its own owner. Build once, copy everywhere."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations on the same pages.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly flatwork price note from shared bids
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short note each month on where yard prices, rebar and dump fees are heading, built only from tickets contractors share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Contractors re-price constantly, and contributed data keeps the note honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Tool and mixer rental yard booking site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Concrete crews rent power trowels, saws and mixers by phone. A booking site with live availability is how the rental yard keeps them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Rental yards serve every flatwork crew in town and the concrete client knows exactly what goes wrong at the counter.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Finisher apprenticeship recruiting page for training centres
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The trade school or training centre
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Concrete outfits can't find finishers, and the training centre can't fill seats. A recruiting page that shows real driveway crews helps both."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training centres have enrolment budgets, and the concrete client is a willing employer partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Exclusive concrete client in each new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A concrete contractor in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one driveway contractor per metro, so the finish gallery and estimator stay yours. The next metro's slot is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing territory lets you reuse the whole concrete stack and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The concrete contractor stuck with a broken site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your old web person left you with a site that can't take a quote request. I can move you onto the concrete template another contractor already runs on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already chose to spend. They want someone with finished concrete sites to point at.

upsellLadder.offer: Concrete site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The concrete site and the care plan sit on one contract, so posting a new stamped driveway is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review texts after cure plus Google profile posts
upsellLadder.trigger: The first driveway poured since launch has cured and the customer has parked on it.
upsellLadder.line: "That driveway's cured and they're parking on it. Now's when they'll write the review, so let's ask."

upsellLadder.trigger: A stamped or coloured pour is on the calendar.
upsellLadder.line: "Your next stamped pour is the one to film. Truck to final pattern makes the best clip you'll post all year."

upsellLadder.offer: Driveway price estimator by size and finish
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of quote forms show the same driveway sizes and finishes asked for repeatedly.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your quote requests are two-car driveways in broom or stamped. Let the estimator give them a range first."

upsellLadder.offer: Crack picture triage on the quote form
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention driving out to look at a crack that only needed sealing.
upsellLadder.line: "That trip to look at a hairline crack is what this stops. The picture tells you which visit to make."

upsellLadder.trigger: A rain week scrambles their pours, or they add a second finishing crew.
upsellLadder.line: "After that rain week, nobody should be rebuilding the pour schedule on paper. One calendar, one tap to move a pour."

upsellLadder.trigger: The earliest stamped jobs since launch approach their first reseal window.
